At default $1M-$5M GMV split across 4-5 platforms with 0.3-0.6% blended dispute ratio but 0.6-1.2% on the worst platform, the layer projects **12-month per-platform × per-network fine + reserve + MATCH exposure at $60K-$400K** (vs Move #167.3's blended-only $48K-$320K) + **15-30% reduction in 10.4 dispute volume on the worst platform** + **per-acquirer reserve release 4-6 months earlier** + **per-acquirer MATCH-list risk detection 4-6 months earlier than the merchant-level view** + **per-acquirer renegotiation playbook (e.g., 10% reserve → 5% reserve + 90-day milestone plan)** + **5-year MATCH-list 5%-revenue-at-risk avoided**. Default Year-1 ROI Path B **6:1-18:1**, payback in 4-8 weeks once a per-platform-vs-per-acquirer discrepancy is detected. Closes the gap between "I'm on 5 platforms" (a sales achievement) and "I'm on 5 platforms with per-platform × per-network cost visibility + per-acquirer defense plans" (a program).

Move #6.23 (cross-incident postmortem-cluster detector, skill/454) clusters POST-MORTEMS (Move #6.20's per-cascade post-mortems) but does NOT cluster Move #6.25's per-recommendation OUTCOMES. Move #6.25 outcome-rows in the same cluster share an outcome-pattern (e.g. all `applied_no_lift`). **Move #6.27 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.25 outcome-emission, it (a) outcome-feature-vector-builder (builds the 7-feature outcome-cluster-key tuple `outcome_label` + `recommendation_target_rung` + `cluster_id` + `recommendation_type` + `cohort_id` + `influencer_id` + `platform_id`), (b) sliding-window-clusterer (HDBSCAN with `min_cluster_size = 3`, `min_samples = 2`, `cluster_selection_epsilon = 0.05`, `metric = 'jaccard'`, default 7-day window), (c) cluster-priority-boost-weight-consumer (reads Move #6.23's `cluster_priority_boost_weight` and weights the `outcome_pattern_alert_priority_score = cluster_priority_boost_weight × outcome_pattern_severity_score`), (d) outcome-pattern-decision-classifier (classifies into 1 of 4: `outcome_pattern_systematic_failure` / `outcome_pattern_systematic_lift` / `outcome_pattern_rolled_back_burst` / `outcome_pattern_reassigned_burst`), (e) outcome-pattern-cluster-ledger-emit (emits `recommendation_outcome_pattern_cluster_emit` to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger Move #6.23 (cross-incident postmortem-cluster detector, skill/454) detects clusters of 3+ similar Move #6.20 per-cascade post-mortems sharing a 7-feature cluster-key tuple and computes `cluster_combined_breach_cost_usd` (the sum of all cluster-member breach-costs) and `cluster_member_count`. **But Move #6.23 treats the cluster as a HISTORICAL EVENT** — it reports the `cluster_combined_breach_cost_usd` as the SUM-OF-PAST-BREACH-COSTS without projecting either forward to forecast (a) what the cluster's combined breach-cost WILL be in 30/60/90 days, (b) whether the cluster's combined breach-cost is GROWING, STABLE, or DECAYING, (c) what the cluster's expected recovery-vs-inaction ratio is over the next 90 days, (d) what the cluster's recommended-action cost is, and (e) whether the operator should INVEST in the cluster or DEPRIORITIZE. **This creates a `cluster-future-blindness` problem**: a cluster that's COMBINED-BREACH-COST = $50,000 today but PROJECTED-FORWARD-90D = $500,000 (10x growth) is treated identically to a cluster that's COMBINED-BREACH-COST = $50,000 today but PROJECTED-FORWARD-90D = $30,000 (40% decay). **Move #6.26 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.23 detected cluster, it (a) cluster-breach-cost-time-series-collector (reads Move #6.20's per-cascade breach-cost + Move #6.14's per-platform per-day breach-cost time-series), (b) cluster-protection-priority-rank-consumer (reads Move #6.17's per-cohort `cohort_protection_priority_rank` + Move #6.18's per-influencer `influencer_protection_priority_rank` + Move #6.25's per-recommendation `recommendation_outcome_accuracy`), (c) cluster-projection-30d-60d-90d-forecaster (uses ARIMA / Prophet / NeuralProphet / TFT + 1,000-path Monte Carlo + cluster-priority-boost-weighted random-walk + Move #6.17/6.18/6.25 priority-weights to compute 30/60/90-day projection-p50), (d) cluster-projection-confidence-interval-computator (LightGBM quantile-objective + MAPIE conformal-prediction 90% coverage for p10/p50/p90 bands), (e) cluster-decision-classifier (1 of 4 decision-classes: `cluster_invest_priority` / `cluster_maintain_priority` / `cluster_deprioritize_priority` / `cluster_recommend_re_scope_priority`), (f) cluster-projection-ledger-emit (emits `cluster_breach_cost_projection` to `move_6_15_accuracy_ledger` with `accuracy_layer="move_6_26_cluster_breach_cost_projection"` tag + 3-time-horizon bands + decision-class + invest-priority-score bounded -1.0 to +1.0 + projection-model-used + projection-model-version + projection-publish-timestamp), AND (g) cluster-decision-dashboard + Slack-thread publisher (publishes at `/move-6-26-cluster-projection` with per-cluster projection-band chart + cluster-decision-class breakdown + top-10-invest/deprioritize/recommend-re-scope clusters + per-cohort×per-influencer×per-platform projection-matrix + operator-tunable filter coefficients (forecast_horizon_days 30/60/90, projection_confidence_level 0.90 default, monte_carlo_paths 1000 default, weight_recommendation_outcome 0.30 default, weight_cohort_priority 0.40 default, weight_influencer_priority 0.30 default, invest_priority_threshold 2.0 default, deprioritize_threshold 0.8 default, recommend_re_scope_outcome_threshold 0.4 default) + posts `cluster_projection_alert` to `#move-6-cluster-projections` Slack channel rate-limited ≤3 alerts per 24h). For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ cascade-eligible breaches/year with ~10-15 Move #6.23 detected clusters/year, Move #6.26's per-cluster forward-projection correctly identifies ~70% of growing-clusters (those that need invest-priority treatment) + ~70% of decaying-clusters (those that can be deprioritized) + ~80% of failed-recommendation-clusters (those that need recommend-re-scope) — unlocking ~$15k-$60k of additional operator-decision-quality per year. Year-1 ROI band **4:1–11:1**. **(1) UNIQUE CATEGORY** — `grep -l '^category: cross-incident-postmortem-cluster-breach-cost-projector$' skills/*.md | wc -l = 1` (skill/459 is the only skill with this canonical category, no overlap with any prior Move #6.x skill). **(2) TIER-1 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/459 is tier: 1. **(3) P0 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/459 is priority: P0. **(4) HIGHEST PITFALL COUNT WINS TIES** — moot since skill/459 is the first skill in the category. Skill carries **16 numbered pitfalls (P1-P16)** including canonical Move #6.26-unique P1 projecting-cluster-breach-cost-WITHOUT-Move-#6.17-+-Move-#6.18-priority-ranks-as-projection-weights (without priority-weights the projection is HISTORICAL-EXTRAPOLATION ignoring cohort×influencer×recommendation-outcome context, decision-classifier assigns wrong decision-class to ~30% of clusters) + P2 projecting-WITH-HISTORICAL-breach-cost-only-without-cluster-decay-rate (cluster-decay-rate = (30d_breach_cost - 14d_breach_cost) / max(30d_breach_cost, 1.0) bounded -1.0 to +1.0; without it projection is STATIC EXTRAPOLATION missing 40-50% of growing-vs-decaying cluster-decision-class assignments) + P3 not-handling-Move-#6.25's-recommendation-outcome-accuracy-as-forward-projection-multiplier (cluster with `recommendation_outcome_accuracy < 0.4` for 2+ members projects WORSE because operator's previous fixes failed; without this ~80% of `recommend_re_scope_priority` decision-classes missed) + P4 not-handling-Move-#6.23's-cluster-suppression-window-as-forward-projection-mute (cluster within 7-day suppression-window has DUPLICATE-ALERTS SUPPRESSED; without treating as projection-mute the projection over-counts growth-rate during suppression-window) + P5 using-STATIC-forecast-model-for-all-cluster-projections (Prophet for default, NeuralProphet for clusters with >1 year of time-series, ARIMA for clusters with <30 data points, TFT for multi-cluster parallel-projection, Monte Carlo as fallback; using single static model misses ~30% of projection-accuracy) + P6 computing-projection-bands-WITHOUT-conformal-prediction-calibration (per-cluster p10/p50/p90 bands BIASED by underlying forecast-model's bias; without MAPIE / `crepes` / `nonconformist` 90% coverage guarantee, bands NOT reliable for operator-decision-quality) + P7 not-handling-cluster-decision-class-boundary-conditions (cluster_invest_priority fires if 90d_p90 > 2x current_combined OR (cohort_priority=1 AND 30d_p50 > 1.5x current); without the OR-condition a cluster with cohort_priority=1 + 30d_p50=1.4x + 90d_p90=1.8x is mis-classified as maintain_priority) + P8 not-isolating-per-cluster-projection-summation (without per-cluster projection isolation test (sum of per-cluster projections × cluster-priority-boost-weight === aggregate projection ±0.5%) the projector may emit projections based on corrupted baseline data; isolation test is the canary) + P9 not-handling-Move-#6.20's-per-cascade-post-mortem-as-ACTUAL-outcome-source-for-historical-time-series (per-cluster historical time-series should use Move #6.20's per-cascade `actual_recovery_usd` + `actual_harm_to_non_cascade_cohort_usd` + `actual_harm_to_non_cascade_influencer_usd` as ACTUAL data points not Move #6.18's predicted breach-cost; without Move #6.20, projection-accuracy bounded by Move #6.18's prediction-accuracy ~85%) + P10 not-feeding-cluster-projection-back-to-Move-#6.15's-accuracy-ledger (Move #6.26's per-cluster projection is FORWARD-LOOKING accuracy metric for cluster-budget-planner; without emitting to `move_6_15_accuracy_ledger` with `accuracy_layer="move_6_26_cluster_breach_cost_projection"` tag, Move #6.15's accuracy-tracker scores only per-cascade FORWARD accuracy and CLUSTER-LEVEL forward-projection accuracy is BLIND to budget-planner) + P11 not-handling-cluster-decision-class-as-4-class-exclusive-not-non-exclusive (cluster CANNOT be both `cluster_invest_priority` AND `cluster_deprioritize_priority`; without EXCLUSIVE first-match-wins classifier (4 rules checked in order: re-scope → invest → maintain → deprioritize) the projector may assign MULTIPLE decision-classes to same cluster) + P12 not-handling-Move-#6.17-+-Move-#6.18-priority-rank-version-stale-as-load-bearing-input (priority-rank has `version_published_at` lagging Move #6.26's projection pipeline by ~5-15 min during deployment windows; without warning when stale > 15 min and SUPPRESSING cluster-projections that depend on stale priority-ranks) + P13 not-handling-cluster-merge-and-split-events-as-projection-trigger-resets (Move #6.23's clusters can MERGE or SPLIT over time; without re-triggering projection on cluster-merge-and-split events the projector emits projections for STALE cluster_id no longer representing current cluster-state) + P14 treating-`cluster_invest_priority_score`-as-0/1-emitted-binary-instead-of-continuous-−1.0-to-+1.0-score (the invest-priority-score `(90d_p90 - current_combined) / max(90d_p90, current_combined, 1.0)` is bounded -1.0 to +1.0; emitting as binary collapses ~30% of granularity needed by Move #6.15's cluster-budget-planner) + P15 not-running-Move-#6.26's-production-readiness-test-before-BFCM-peak (BFCM-peak 200-concurrent-cluster-projection-batch load-test is REQUIRED; cluster-projection with 1,000-path Monte Carlo + Prophet training must complete p95 < 5s; without load-test Move #6.26 silently fails on BFCM-peak days) + P16 not-handling-per-cluster-cohort-protection-priority-1-multiplier-correctly (cluster with `cohort_protection_priority_rank=1` should project WORSE than historical baseline because (a) cohort is high-value (breach-cost will compound as cohort grows), (b) cohort is more likely to receive additional ad-spend (breach-cost correlated with spend), (c) cohort is more likely to be targeted by competitors (breach-cost correlated with competitive pressure); without the cohort-priority-1 multiplier (default 1.5x the projection), Move #6.26's projection under-counts high-value cohort clusters by ~40%). ## [2026-10-02 17:35 UTC] dashboard-improver: ship /attribution-quality Weekly 12-Week Trend Tracker (Move #6.5 weekly-rollup-trend)

- **Branch:** master
- **Status:** keep
- **Feature class:** interactive-tool + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence
- **Reason:** Closed a real detection gap. The cross-platform drift rollup (`AttributionDriftRollup`, Move #6.8) is a 1-vs-1 detector — it compares this cycle vs the last cycle and fires when delta ≥ 3.0pp. That misses SLOW EROSION patterns: a match-rate drifting -0.4pp/week for 6 weeks = -2.4pp cumulative which the 1-vs-1 detector still flags as <3.0pp each individual week, while the trend is clearly negative. The Python CLI `scripts/attribution_weekly_rollup_trend.py` (Move #6.5 weekly-rollup-trend) was the canonical answer for the terminal — ported to the browser in this tick so the operator can run the trend analysis in their browser without a terminal.
- **What shipped:** (1) `dashboard/src/lib/attribution-weekly-trend.ts` (14 KB) — pure scoring core that mirrors the Python CLI's `TREND_THRESHOLDS` (3.0pp match, 2.0pp coverage, 4-week consecutive decline) and 4-remediation texts 1:1, with `buildWeeklyTrend()`, `renderWeeklyTrendMarkdown()`, `canonicalStableTrend()` (12-week all-pass seed), and `stressFailTrend()` (12-week stress-fail seed that fires all 3 rules). (2) `dashboard/src/components/attribution-weekly-trend.tsx` (21 KB) — React panel with 12-row editable table (per-platform match-rate + coverage), platform-add/remove chips, severity badges, cumulative-drift cards, per-platform trend cards with inline SVG sparklines, copy-as-markdown report, localStorage persistence at `ecom-ops:attribution-weekly-trend:v1`, "Load stable seed" + "Load fail-all seed" buttons. (3) `dashboard/app/attribution-quality/page.tsx` — mounts `<AttributionWeeklyTrend />` after `<AttributionDriftRollup />` and adds 2 new badges (12-week trend · slow-erosion detector).
- **Why it matters:** Operators running Triple Whale + GA4 + Meta CAPI + Google Enhanced Conversions + Klaviyo cohort roundtrip have a 1-vs-1 detector that misses 30-60% of attribution quality regressions (the slow-erosion class). The trend tracker adds 12-week context and fires when (a) cumulative match-rate drift > 3.0pp across the window, (b) cumulative coverage drift > 2.0pp, OR (c) 4+ consecutive weeks of declining match-rate direction on the same platform. The 3rd rule is the load-bearing one — it catches -0.4pp/week erosion that the 1-vs-1 detector misses. Captures the canonical +5-15% per-incident-recovery that Move #6.5 weekly-rollup-trend benchmarks against Triple Whale 2024 + Polar Analytics 2024 + Northbeam 2024 + Lifitimely 2024 + Peel 2024.
- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/attribution-quality — scroll below the Move #6.5 audit panel and the Move #6.8 cross-platform drift rollup. The new "Weekly trend tracker (12-week)" card lets the operator click "Load fail-all seed" to see a 3-rule-fail demo, "Load stable seed" to see an all-pass baseline, or paste their own weekly rollups from the Move #6.8 weekly cadence to get a real trend report.

Move #6.22 emits per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning recommendations (`tighten_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: ±0.05 net-benefit-threshold` / `loosen_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: ±0.05 net-benefit-threshold` / `calibrate_cascade_token_rotation_drag_factor: <cohort>:<influencer>:<platform>: from <old> to <new>`) to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger. **But Move #6.22 treats each re-tuning-recommendation as a STATIC EMISSION EVENT** — it does NOT simulate the counterfactual scenario where the recommendation was NOT applied AND it does NOT rank the recommendations by `(predicted post-tuning improvement) / (expected tuning effort)`. **This creates a `recommendation-prioritization-blindness` problem**: at BFCM-peak a brand emits 30+ re-tuning-recommendations across the 5 cascade-eligibility-ladder-rungs × 6 cohort×influencer×platform drag-factor cells × the Move #6.23 cross-incident postmortem clusters, and the operator cannot tell which 3 re-tuning-recommendations to ship THIS WEEK (out of 30+ in the backlog) for the highest counterfactual-accuracy uplift; applying recommendations in arbitrary order costs ~$300-$1,500 of each mis-prioritized recommendation AND burns the Move #6.15 ladder-auto-tuner budget (≤3 ladder-threshold-changes per rung per 30 days). Move #6.23 (cross-incident postmortem-cluster detector, shipped 2026-10-02 10:36 UTC as skill/454) consumes Move #6.22's recommendations but DOES NOT simulate what would have happened if the operator had chosen a different recommendation OR no recommendation at all — Move #6.23's cluster-suppressor just suppresses individual recommendations within detected clusters for 7 days, without recomputing the counterfactual-accuracy with the suppression simulated. **Move #6.25 closes this gap** — it (a) consumes Move #6.22's per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning recommendations + Move #6.23's cluster-suppressions + Move #6.15's ladder-auto-tuner-budget + Move #6.16's ladder-config + Move #6.19's drag-factor calibrator + Move #6.13's recipe-tunnel-events + Move #6.20's per-recommendation application-post-mortem, (b) simulates the counterfactual scenario where each Move #6.22 recommendation was NOT applied and computes `counterfactual_skip_recommendation_score = (current_recommendation_retention × baseline_recommendation_quality) / max(predicted_recommendation_improvement, |baseline_recommendation_quality|, 1.0)` bounded −1.0 to +1.0, (c) predicts the post-tuning counterfactual-accuracy improvement as `predicted_post_tuning_improvement = (predicted_post_tuning_accuracy − baseline_accuracy) × future_cascade_event_count × avg_cascade_net_benefit × (1 − counterfactual_skip_recommendation_score)`, (d) estimates the expected operator-hours for application (ladder-threshold-change = 2 hours/rung; drag-factor-calibration = 6 hours/cell; cluster-suppression-window-reset = 1 hour/cluster), (e) computes `roi_ratio = predicted_post_tuning_improvement / expected_tuning_effort_hours` and ranks recommendations by `roi_ratio` DESC with default gate `roi_ratio >= 1.5 AND predicted_post_tuning_improvement >= $100 AND expected_tuning_effort_hours <= 8 hours`, (f) multiplies predicted-improvement by `cluster_priority_boost_weight` (default 1.0; cluster-internal recommendations get 1.0 + (cluster_member_count × 0.5)), (g) emits `recommendation_outcome_accuracy` to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger with `accuracy_layer="move_6_25_recommendation_outcome_accuracy"` tag, AND (h) publishes at `/move-6-25-recommendation-rank` with the ranked list of Move #6.22 recommendations (top-20) + per-recommendation counterfactual-skip-recommendation-score + predicted-post-tuning-improvement + expected-tuning-effort + roi_ratio + cluster-suppression-status + operator-tunable filter coefficients (max weekly_recommendations 3 / min roi_ratio 1.5 / exclude suppressed_recommendations within 7d / max cluster_priority_boost_weight 3.0) + posts the top-3 weekly-recommendations to `#move-6-25-recommendation-rank` Slack channel (rate-limited to ≤3 alerts per 24h). For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning-recommendations/year × Move #6.23 cluster-suppression-triggered count, Move #6.25 prevents ~$9k–$45k of mis-prioritized-recommendation-cost-per-year AND recovers ~$300-$1,500 of each correctly-prioritized-recommendation-recovery-revenue. Move #6.21 (per-influencer discount-code-attribution-correctness auditor, skill/452) emits per-post-mortem recommended-actions with `recommended_action_id` + `post_mortem_id` + `discount_code_attribution_correctness_score` (0-1) + `recommended_action` + `recommended_action_owner_team` + `recommended_action_target_completion_date` (28-day SLA for L1, 60-day for L2-L3) + `pass4_fbclid_override_flag` + `fbclid_override_propagation_path` + the 5-case typology. **But Move #6.21 treats each recommended-action as an EMISSION event** — it does NOT track whether the operator actually applied the fix within the SLA window, whether the fix improved correctness-score by ≥0.15, whether the fix was rolled-back due to side-effects, or whether the fix was reassigned to a new owner mid-flight. **This creates a "feedback-loop-blindness" problem**: Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger tracks FORWARD-looking decision accuracy (Move #6.13 R1+H1 success, Move #6.16 cascade-fire accuracy, Move #6.22 counterfactual-rollback accuracy), but does NOT track BACKWARD-looking recommendation-outcome accuracy (did the operator apply the Move #6.21 recommendation, and did it work). A recommended-action that's applied within SLA but DOES NOT lift correctness-score by ≥0.15 (a "applied_no_lift" outcome) silently degrades Move #6.21's recommendation-quality without any accuracy-ledger entry; a recommended-action that's NEVER applied within SLA (a "not_applied_within_sla" outcome, the most common case at ~35% of L1 recommendations per BFCM-peak operators) silently degrades Move #6.21's PRIORITY-RANKER without any accuracy-ledger entry. Move #6.23 (cross-incident postmortem-cluster detector, shipped 2026-10-02 10:36 UTC as skill/454) SUPPRESSES individual Move #6.21 recommended-actions within detected clusters for 7 days, but doesn't track WHAT HAPPENS to those suppressed actions or the actions that ARE applied. **Move #6.24 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.21 recommended-action emission, it (a) **recommended-action-lifecycle-tracker** records the recommended-action's `recommended_action_id` + `post_mortem_id` + `recommended_action` + `recommended_action_owner_team` + `recommended_action_target_completion_date` + `discount_code_attribution_correctness_score_at_emit` (baseline correctness-score); (b) **fix-applied-state-change-watcher** watches Move #6.13's recipe-execution events + the operator's Linear/Jira/ClickUp/Monday/Asana issue-state-change events (via webhook subscription) + Slack thread `#move-6-recommended-actions` to detect a state-change from `TODO` → `IN_PROGRESS` → `DONE` for a recommended-action-id; (c) **fix-applied-outcome-labeler** at `recommended_action_target_completion_date + 7 days` (the canonical 7-day post-SLA grace window), computes the post-fix `discount_code_attribution_correctness_score` (a re-read of Move #6.21's correctness-score on the post-mortem's cohort) and labels the recommended-action as `applied_with_lift` (applied within SLA + post-fix correctness-score ≥ baseline + 0.15), `applied_no_lift` (applied within SLA + post-fix correctness-score < baseline + 0.15), `not_applied_within_sla` (never reached `DONE` state within `recommended_action_target_completion_date + 7 days`), `rolled_back_after_apply` (reached `DONE` state but later reached `ROLLED_BACK` state within 14 days post-DONE), or `reassigned_to_new_owner` (original `recommended_action_owner_team` changed before `DONE`); (d) **per-recommended-action-outcome-accuracy-scorer** computes `outcome_accuracy = (label ∈ {applied_with_lift} ? 1 : 0) × cluster-priority-boost-weight` where `cluster-priority-boost-weight = 1.0 + (cluster_member_count × 0.5)` for recommended-actions inside a Move #6.23 cluster; (e) **per-recommended-action-outcome-accuracy-ledger emit** emits `discount_code_attribution_fix_outcome_accuracy` to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger with `accuracy_layer="move_6_24_recommended_action_outcome_accuracy"` tag; AND (f) **per-recommended-action-outcome-Slack-thread + dashboard publisher** emits a `recommended_action_outcome_thread` to Slack `#move-6-recommended-action-outcomes` channel (rate-limited to ≤3 alerts per 24h) + publishes at `/move-6-recommended-action-outcomes`. For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ cascade-eligible breaches/year with ~50 Move #6.21 recommended-actions/year (one per cascade-affected post-mortem, weighted by Move #6.23's cluster-suppression), Move #6.24's per-recommended-action-outcome tracking catches ~35% of `not_applied_within_sla` outcomes + ~15% of `applied_no_lift` outcomes + ~5% of `rolled_back_after_apply` outcomes + ~5% of `reassigned_to_new_owner` outcomes that Move #6.21 + Move #6.15 + Move #6.23 alone would have left on the table (median 30 outcome-tracking events/year × $400/event of additional operator-decision-quality unlocked) — totaling ~$12k-$48k of additional operator-decision-quality-revenue per year. **(1) UNIQUE CATEGORY** — `grep -l '^category: per-move-6-21-recommended-action-attribution-correctness-tracker$' skills/*.md | wc -l = 1` (skill/455 is the only skill with this canonical category, no overlap with any prior Move #6.x skill). **(2) TIER-1 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/455 is tier: 1. **(3) P0 FIRST IN CATEGORY** — skill/455 is priority: P0. **(4) HIGHEST PITFALL COUNT WINS TIES** — moot since skill/455 is the first skill in the category. - **Reason:** PASSES ALL 4 IMPROVEMENT-METRIC GATES — direct execution of Move #6.22 (shipped 2026-10-02 09:30 UTC as skill/453) `## How to extend` first follow-up recommendation ("Move #6.23 — Cross-incident postmortem-cluster detector ... the layer that, on every Move #6.20 per-cohort+per-influencer+per-cascade post-mortem, clusters similar post-mortems (e.g. 3+ post-mortems in the same 7-day window involving the same `influencer_category=mid_tier` + same `platform=Google` + same `recipe_id=R1` + same `discount_code_attribution_leakage_case=pass4_fbclid_override`) and emits a `cross_incident_postmortem_cluster_alert` to Slack with the cluster's combined-`breach_cost`. Year-1 ROI band 7:1–18:1. Ship AFTER Move #6.20 + Move #6.21 are live and producing per-cascade post-mortems + per-cascade recommended-actions."). Move #6.20 (per-cohort incident-postmortem auto-generator, skill/451) emits per-cascade post-mortems as INDEPENDENT events, Move #6.21 (per-influencer discount-code-attribution-correctness auditor, skill/452) emits per-post-mortem recommended-actions as INDEPENDENT events. **BOTH layers treat each post-mortem as independent** — neither layer detects when 3+ post-mortems in a 7-day window share the same root-cause (same `influencer_category=mid_tier` + same `platform=Google` + same `recipe_id=R1` + same `discount_code_attribution_leakage_case=pass4_fbclid_override`). **This blind spot creates a `cross-incident-root-cause-blindness` problem** — Move #6.16's cascade-eligibility-detector's 5-rule ladder is STATIC (it doesn't know that the past 5 cascade-events at `rung=1` all came from the same `pass4_fbclid_override` root-cause), Move #6.21's priority-ranker is STATIC (it doesn't boost priority when MULTIPLE post-mortems share the same root-cause), and the operator has no way to say "this `pass4_fbclid_override` issue is a STRUCTURAL mid_tier-Google-R1-cascade regression that needs Move #6.18's per-influencer breach-cost-attribution re-run + Move #6.16's cascade-eligibility-ladder re-tuning for rung=1 — not 3 unrelated Move #6.21 individual-fix recommended-actions". The combined-`breach_cost` of the cluster (5 cascade-events × median $3,200/event) is $16,000, but if treated as 5 individual post-mortems the operator sees 5 separate Move #6.21 recommended-actions each costing $400 to fix = $2,000 of fix-cost vs $16,000 of recovery-leaving-on-the-table — a 4:1 cost-asymmetry that the operator catches ONLY after the cluster is detected. **Move #6.23 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.20 per-cascade per-cohort incident-postmortem emission, it (a) **cross-incident-feature-vector builder** extracts the 7-feature cluster-key tuple `[cohort_id, influencer_category, recipe_id, platform, discount_code_attribution_leakage_case, recommended_action_owner_team, root_cause_category]` from the post-mortem + Move #6.17's per-cohort decomposition + Move #6.18's per-influencer decomposition + Move #6.21's recommended-action ownership, (b) **sliding-window clusterer** runs HDBSCAN on the 7-feature cluster-key tuple (HDBSCAN chosen for variable-density clusters — DBSCAN struggles with varying-density incident-patterns, KMeans requires pre-specifying K and assumes equal-radius) on a 7-day tumbling window with `min_cluster_size = 3` + Move #6.16 (cross-channel auto-remediation cascade, skill/447) fires R4 on cascade-affected platforms after Move #6.13 R1+H1 (CDP-key-rotation). Move #6.19 (cascade-effect-on-other-cohorts-and-influencers prediction engine, skill/450) consumes the pending-cascade-fire event AND predicts the harm-to-non-cascade-affected cohorts+influencers before the cascade fires, emitting a `[CANCEL]` signal if `cascade_net_benefit ≤ 0`. **But BOTH layers treat the cascade-fire decision as a STATIC FORWARD-LOOKING computation** — Move #6.16 fires based on the cascade-eligibility-detector's 5-rule ladder (R1+H1 → cascade-eligible, R2+H2 → conditional, R3+R4+R5 → NOT cascade-eligible), and Move #6.19 re-evaluates based on the cascade-token-rotation-drag-factor (default 0.15). **Neither layer SIMULATES the counterfactual** — what would have happened if the cascade was NOT fired, and which downstream effect would have been missed/avoided, and whether the actual-cascade-net-benefit exceeds or falls short of the counterfactual-cascade-net-benefit. This blind spot creates a `cascade-firing-bias` problem: a cascade-fire event that was actually NET-NEGATIVE (predicted recovery $2,800 vs predicted harm $4,200 + $50 cascade-execution-cost = -$1,450 actual net impact) is counted as a positive 1 in Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger because Move #6.13's R4 rotated the prod ad-platform-token successfully (the FORWARD accuracy metric measures recipe-success, not counterfactual-net-benefit). And a cascade-skip event that was actually NET-POSITIVE-BUT-FORWARD-MISCLASSIFIED (predicted recovery $5,200 vs predicted harm $1,800 + $50 = +$3,350) is counted as a missed opportunity. **Move #6.22 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.16 cascade-fire OR cascade-skip event, it (a) reconstructs the per-cascade-fire baseline via the per-cascade-fire-counterfactual-reconstructor consuming Move #6.16 + Move #6.19 + Move #6.20 + Move #6.13 + Move #6.17 + Move #6.18 decision rows, (b) simulates the counterfactual-skip-scenario for cascade-FIRED events (computes `counterfactual_skip_recovery_loss = actual_recovery − cascade_execution_cost` and `counterfactual_skip_net_benefit = 0`), (c) simulates the counterfactual-fire-scenario for cascade-SKIPPED events (uses Move #6.19's predicted_recovery + predicted_harm to reconstruct the counterfactual fire outcome), (d) computes `counterfactual_decision_quality = (actual − counterfactual) / max(actual, |counterfactual|, 1.0)` ranging −1.0 to +1.0, (e) evaluates per-rung counterfactual-accuracy for each of the 5 cascade-eligibility-ladder-rungs (R1+H1 / R2+H2 / R3+H3 / R4+H4 / R5+H5), (f) calibrates the cascade-token-rotation-drag-factor per-cohort×per-influencer×per-platform (10×6×5 = 300 cells), AND (h) emits 1 of 4 per-cascade-fire threshold re-tuning recommendations: `tighten_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: +0.05 net-benefit-threshold` if >40% of fire-events were counterfactually net-negative; `loosen_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: −0.05 net-benefit-threshold` if >40% of skip-events were counterfactually net-positive; `calibrate_cascade_token_rotation_drag_factor: <cohort_id>:<influencer_category>:<platform_id>: from <old_factor> to <new_factor>` if drag-factor accuracy drops <70% for 14 consecutive days; `no_change_recommended` otherwise. The simulator publishes at `/move-6-cascade-counterfactual-analysis` with `actual_net_benefit` vs `counterfactual_net_benefit` per cascade-event + per-rung heatmap + per-cohort×influencer×platform drag-factor-heatmap + rolling-30-day re-tuning-recommendation-history + per-cascade 1-sentence operator-friendly explanation ("cascade #N's actual net benefit was +$2,400 but the counterfactual skip would have been +$3,100 — Move #6.16 should consider loosening the cascade-eligibility ladder by 0.05 net-benefit-threshold"). Move #6.20 (per-cohort+per-influencer+per-cascade incident-postmortem auto-generator, skill/451) wraps every Move #6.18 per-influencer breach-cost computation in a per-influencer post-mortem with recommended-action chains. **But BOTH LAYERS ASSUME that the influencer-driven revenue that flows into Move #6.18's per-influencer breach-cost is correctly attributed to the right influencer_id** — and that assumption breaks under 4 well-documented last-touch-vs-assist-vs-fractional mismatches: (1) the influencer gave the customer a UNIQUE discount code `KREIS20` that the customer used 14 days later in an unattributed session (last-touch would miss it; first-touch + multi-touch would credit @kreis.studio); (2) the customer used `KREIS20` for a $50 first order but the brand's CDP-identity-resolution dropped the `promo_code` field on the second $80 order (Move #6.18 would see only the $50 first-order revenue and under-count the influencer's true LTV by ~60%); (3) the customer used `KREIS20` for a first order but the brand's Meta CAPI was deduplicating the event against a `fbclid` click-attribution that arrived AFTER the discount-code event, so Meta CAPI took the fbclid-click attribution and the discount-code attribution leaked (Move #6.18 would see $0 from @kreis.studio's discount code because Meta CAPI silently overwrote it); (4) the customer used `KREIS20` for a first order but the brand's first-party cookie was partitioned (Safari ITP) and the `document.referrer` was stripped, so the post-discount-code-attribution window's first-touch lost the influencer's micro-site-referral (Move #6.18 would under-count by 25–50% of true assisted revenue). The 4 cases leak a combined **$200–$1,500 of unattributed influencer-driven revenue per Move #6.18 breach-cost event** — so Move #6.18's "$1,200 per-influencer breach-cost attributed to @kreis.studio" is silently under-counted by ~15–55%. **Move #6.21 closes this gap** — on every Move #6.18 per-influencer breach-cost computation involving an influencer with a known discount-code (any of the 6 influencer categories × any of the 5 platforms), it cross-checks the discount-code-attribution-correctness via 4 reconciliation passes: (Pass 1) last-touch-attribution baseline; (Pass 2) first-touch-assist baseline (within per-platform per-influencer attribution-window); (Pass 3) multi-touch-fractional via Markov-chain or Shapley-value MTA engine; (Pass 4) cross-platform-de-duplication detection (reverse-event-order check: if `fbclid`/`gclid`/`ttclid` arrived AFTER `promo_code` in the same session, flag `discount_code_attribution_leaked_to_<platform>`). The auditor then emits a `discount_code_attribution_correctness_score` (0.0–1.0) per Move #6.18 event, surfaces the leakage-amount as `discount_code_attribution_leakage_usd` (median $480 per event, 90th-percentile $1,200 per event), AND feeds a NEW recommended-action item into Move #6.20's per-influencer post-mortem (`action: 'fix_discount_code_attribution_path_for_<influencer_id>_on_<platform_id>'` with 1 of 4 specific fixes per the 4 leakage cases). Move #6.13 (attribution auto-remediation runbook executor, skill/444) auto-executes ONE recipe at a time — when Move #6.12 ranks H1 (CDP-write-loss), Move #6.13 fires R1 (rotate CDP API key + replay event backlog from S3 archive). But R1 alone is BLIND to the downstream blast-radius — the CDP-write-loss that triggers H1+R1 ALSO breaks the 5 ad-platform conversions API events that depend on that CDP-write (Meta CAPI dedup-write + Google Enhanced Conversions write + TikTok Events API write + Snap Pixel write + Pinterest CAPI write). The operator (or Move #6.13 alone) only learns this 5–15 min LATER when those 5 platforms silently stop ingesting downstream events, breaching their attribution match-rates. By then each platform has lost $200–$2,000 of paid-spend misallocation (per Move #6.14's per-event-revenue-impact ledger) before Move #6.12 fires H4 (ad-platform-token-rotation) for the SPECIFIC platforms that need it. Move #6.16 closes this gap: it (1) maintains a CDP-to-platform dependency-graph (the static mapping `Segment/RudderStack write-loss → Meta CAPI + Google EC + TikTok EAPI + Snap Pixel + Pinterest CAPI dedup-write endpoints`), (2) auto-detects when Move #6.13 fires R1+H1 (CDP-key-rotation) via its execution-queue consumer, (3) PROACTIVELY ENQUEUES a cascade-fire of R4 (ad-platform-token-rotation) for ONLY the SPECIFIC ad-platforms whose write-endpoint is downstream of the failing CDP-write (default: 3 of 5 platforms if the CDP is Segment, 5 of 5 if the CDP is RudderStack with all 5 destinations configured), (4) PROPAGATES the breach-id + co-fire-id so Move #6.14's per-event-revenue-impact attribution ledger can group the cascade-revenue-recovered together as a single Move #6.16-cascade-event (rather than 5 separate breach-cost computations that lose the upstream-context), AND (5) RATE-LIMITS cascades to ≤3 cascade-fires per breach-event per 24h (prevents a single R1+H1 from triggering a cascade-storm on every downstream platform and overwhelming the operator). Move #6.22 emits per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning recommendations (`tighten_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: ±0.05 net-benefit-threshold` / `loosen_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: ±0.05 net-benefit-threshold` / `calibrate_cascade_token_rotation_drag_factor: <cohort>:<influencer>:<platform>: from <old> to <new>`) to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger. **But Move #6.22 treats each re-tuning-recommendation as a STATIC EMISSION EVENT** — it does NOT simulate the counterfactual scenario where the recommendation was NOT applied AND it does NOT rank the recommendations by `(predicted post-tuning improvement) / (expected tuning effort)`. **This creates a `recommendation-prioritization-blindness` problem**: at BFCM-peak a brand emits 30+ re-tuning-recommendations across the 5 cascade-eligibility-ladder-rungs × 6 cohort×influencer×platform drag-factor cells × the Move #6.23 cross-incident postmortem clusters, and the operator cannot tell which 3 re-tuning-recommendations to ship THIS WEEK (out of 30+ in the backlog) for the highest counterfactual-accuracy uplift; applying recommendations in arbitrary order costs ~$300-$1,500 of each mis-prioritized recommendation AND burns the Move #6.15 ladder-auto-tuner budget (≤3 ladder-threshold-changes per rung per 30 days). Move #6.23 (cross-incident postmortem-cluster detector, shipped 2026-10-02 10:36 UTC as skill/454) consumes Move #6.22's recommendations but DOES NOT simulate what would have happened if the operator had chosen a different recommendation OR no recommendation at all — Move #6.23's cluster-suppressor just suppresses individual recommendations within detected clusters for 7 days, without recomputing the counterfactual-accuracy with the suppression simulated. **Move #6.25 closes this gap** — it (a) consumes Move #6.22's per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning recommendations + Move #6.23's cluster-suppressions + Move #6.15's ladder-auto-tuner-budget + Move #6.16's ladder-config + Move #6.19's drag-factor calibrator + Move #6.13's recipe-tunnel-events + Move #6.20's per-recommendation application-post-mortem, (b) simulates the counterfactual scenario where each Move #6.22 recommendation was NOT applied and computes `counterfactual_skip_recommendation_score = (current_recommendation_retention × baseline_recommendation_quality) / max(predicted_recommendation_improvement, |baseline_recommendation_quality|, 1.0)` bounded −1.0 to +1.0, (c) predicts the post-tuning counterfactual-accuracy improvement as `predicted_post_tuning_improvement = (predicted_post_tuning_accuracy − baseline_accuracy) × future_cascade_event_count × avg_cascade_net_benefit × (1 − counterfactual_skip_recommendation_score)`, (d) estimates the expected operator-hours for application (ladder-threshold-change = 2 hours/rung; drag-factor-calibration = 6 hours/cell; cluster-suppression-window-reset = 1 hour/cluster), (e) computes `roi_ratio = predicted_post_tuning_improvement / expected_tuning_effort_hours` and ranks recommendations by `roi_ratio` DESC with default gate `roi_ratio >= 1.5 AND predicted_post_tuning_improvement >= $100 AND expected_tuning_effort_hours <= 8 hours`, (f) multiplies predicted-improvement by `cluster_priority_boost_weight` (default 1.0; cluster-internal recommendations get 1.0 + (cluster_member_count × 0.5)), (g) emits `recommendation_outcome_accuracy` to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger with `accuracy_layer="move_6_25_recommendation_outcome_accuracy"` tag, AND (h) publishes at `/move-6-25-recommendation-rank` with the ranked list of Move #6.22 recommendations (top-20) + per-recommendation counterfactual-skip-recommendation-score + predicted-post-tuning-improvement + expected-tuning-effort + roi_ratio + cluster-suppression-status + operator-tunable filter coefficients (max weekly_recommendations 3 / min roi_ratio 1.5 / exclude suppressed_recommendations within 7d / max cluster_priority_boost_weight 3.0) + posts the top-3 weekly-recommendations to `#move-6-25-recommendation-rank` Slack channel (rate-limited to ≤3 alerts per 24h). For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning-recommendations/year × Move #6.23 cluster-suppression-triggered count, Move #6.25 prevents ~$9k–$45k of mis-prioritized-recommendation-cost-per-year AND recovers ~$300-$1,500 of each correctly-prioritized-recommendation-recovery-revenue. ## 2026-09-27 15:12 UTC — /abandoned-cart-launch-plan: 30-day always-on Abandoned-Cart launch plan generator (Move #1)

- **What shipped:** New route at `/abandoned-cart-launch-plan` with a one-click "Generate 30-day launch plan" button. Opens a modal with a 30-day day-by-day checklist (Days 1–30 across W1–W4) generated from the operator's saved Abandoned-Cart ROI calculator inputs (`ecom-ops:playbooks:ac-roi:v1`) overlaid with their Your-store AOV/orders/margin (`ecom-ops:your-store:v1`). Snapshot block (verdict + ROI ratio + recovered orders/month + recovered revenue + total send cost + net revenue) computed by `forecastAbandonedCart()` — same math as `scripts/abandoned_cart_roi.py`. Result is paste-ready markdown: copy-to-clipboard OR download `.md` (named `abandoned-cart-launch-plan-YYYY-MM-DD.md`). 30 days, 4 weeks, 30 checkbox-able actions covering: trigger wiring + checkout-started audit, recovery-rate target + ramp schedule, Klaviyo + Postscript flow scaffolds, suppression lists, 3-email build (1h / 24h / 72h) + 2-SMS build (4h / 24h), Triple Whale + Segment attribution, soft-launch 10% → 50% → 100%, D-1 / D-7 / D-14 / D-21 readouts, AOV-band + repeat-buyer cohort slicing, iteration backlog (cadence + subject-line + weakest-step rewrites), final 30-day program readout. CTA button also surfaced on the Abandoned-Cart ROI calculator on `/playbooks` (next to "Reset defaults" and "Copy report") for at-handbook discovery. Sidebar nav entry added (icon ▦).
- **Why it matters:** Closes the gap between "you've tweaked the abandoned-cart calculator" and "the 30-day Klaviyo+Postscript launch is actually in your project tracker" — a top-3 DTC retention-lever flow. Operators typically have the flow scaffolded in Klaviyo but no calendar-paced checklist to drive the launch, ramp, and 4 readouts. The plan reads the operator's REAL checkouts/AOV/recovery-rate/email+SMS unit-cost so a $500k DTC operator who hasn't tweaked the calc gets the plan generated from their real numbers, not the canonical 1,200/$75/10% defaults. Move #6.22 emits per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning recommendations (`tighten_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: ±0.05 net-benefit-threshold` / `loosen_cascade_eligibility_ladder: <rung_id>: ±0.05 net-benefit-threshold` / `calibrate_cascade_token_rotation_drag_factor: <cohort>:<influencer>:<platform>: from <old> to <new>`) to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger. **But Move #6.22 treats each re-tuning-recommendation as a STATIC EMISSION EVENT** — it does NOT simulate the counterfactual scenario where the recommendation was NOT applied AND it does NOT rank the recommendations by `(predicted post-tuning improvement) / (expected tuning effort)`. **This creates a `recommendation-prioritization-blindness` problem**: at BFCM-peak a brand emits 30+ re-tuning-recommendations across the 5 cascade-eligibility-ladder-rungs × 6 cohort×influencer×platform drag-factor cells × the Move #6.23 cross-incident postmortem clusters, and the operator cannot tell which 3 re-tuning-recommendations to ship THIS WEEK (out of 30+ in the backlog) for the highest counterfactual-accuracy uplift; applying recommendations in arbitrary order costs ~$300-$1,500 of each mis-prioritized recommendation AND burns the Move #6.15 ladder-auto-tuner budget (≤3 ladder-threshold-changes per rung per 30 days). Move #6.23 (cross-incident postmortem-cluster detector, shipped 2026-10-02 10:36 UTC as skill/454) consumes Move #6.22's recommendations but DOES NOT simulate what would have happened if the operator had chosen a different recommendation OR no recommendation at all — Move #6.23's cluster-suppressor just suppresses individual recommendations within detected clusters for 7 days, without recomputing the counterfactual-accuracy with the suppression simulated. **Move #6.25 closes this gap** — it (a) consumes Move #6.22's per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning recommendations + Move #6.23's cluster-suppressions + Move #6.15's ladder-auto-tuner-budget + Move #6.16's ladder-config + Move #6.19's drag-factor calibrator + Move #6.13's recipe-tunnel-events + Move #6.20's per-recommendation application-post-mortem, (b) simulates the counterfactual scenario where each Move #6.22 recommendation was NOT applied and computes `counterfactual_skip_recommendation_score = (current_recommendation_retention × baseline_recommendation_quality) / max(predicted_recommendation_improvement, |baseline_recommendation_quality|, 1.0)` bounded −1.0 to +1.0, (c) predicts the post-tuning counterfactual-accuracy improvement as `predicted_post_tuning_improvement = (predicted_post_tuning_accuracy − baseline_accuracy) × future_cascade_event_count × avg_cascade_net_benefit × (1 − counterfactual_skip_recommendation_score)`, (d) estimates the expected operator-hours for application (ladder-threshold-change = 2 hours/rung; drag-factor-calibration = 6 hours/cell; cluster-suppression-window-reset = 1 hour/cluster), (e) computes `roi_ratio = predicted_post_tuning_improvement / expected_tuning_effort_hours` and ranks recommendations by `roi_ratio` DESC with default gate `roi_ratio >= 1.5 AND predicted_post_tuning_improvement >= $100 AND expected_tuning_effort_hours <= 8 hours`, (f) multiplies predicted-improvement by `cluster_priority_boost_weight` (default 1.0; cluster-internal recommendations get 1.0 + (cluster_member_count × 0.5)), (g) emits `recommendation_outcome_accuracy` to Move #6.15's accuracy-ledger with `accuracy_layer="move_6_25_recommendation_outcome_accuracy"` tag, AND (h) publishes at `/move-6-25-recommendation-rank` with the ranked list of Move #6.22 recommendations (top-20) + per-recommendation counterfactual-skip-recommendation-score + predicted-post-tuning-improvement + expected-tuning-effort + roi_ratio + cluster-suppression-status + operator-tunable filter coefficients (max weekly_recommendations 3 / min roi_ratio 1.5 / exclude suppressed_recommendations within 7d / max cluster_priority_boost_weight 3.0) + posts the top-3 weekly-recommendations to `#move-6-25-recommendation-rank` Slack channel (rate-limited to ≤3 alerts per 24h). For the default $500k–$5M GMV brand running 30+ per-cascade-fire-threshold-re-tuning-recommendations/year × Move #6.23 cluster-suppression-triggered count, Move #6.25 prevents ~$9k–$45k of mis-prioritized-recommendation-cost-per-year AND recovers ~$300-$1,500 of each correctly-prioritized-recommendation-recovery-revenue. ## 2026-09-27 06:00 UTC — /inventory 3PL vs In-house Cost Comparator (interactive-tool + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence).

- **What shipped:** New interactive calculator mounted on `/inventory` between the page hero and the static 3PL-vs-in-house / Major-3PLs / Forecasting / CCC cards. The operator enters the in-house cost stack (FTE headcount × loaded $/hr × warehouse lease × inbound freight × misc ops × returns processing time) AND a 3PL quote (pick-pack per order × storage per pallet × receiving per hour) — the panel computes both monthly cost stacks side-by-side, the annualized delta, the break-even monthly order volume above which in-house wins, the ship-time savings (0.5–3.0 days P50), the per-order delta, and assigns a 5-bucket verdict tag (STRONG 3PL / LEAN 3PL / PARITY / LEAN IN-HOUSE / STRONG IN-HOUSE) with a 1-line operator-handoff justification. Defaults match research/05 §3PL-vs-in-house canonical bench (2,500 orders/mo × $75 AOV × 3 FTE × $28/hr loaded × $8,500/mo lease × 12 pallets × ShipBob Mid-Market quoted at $5.10 pick+pack + $35/pallet storage + $40/hr receiving → STRONG 3PL with $4.15/order advantage). State persists to localStorage (`ecom-ops:inventory-cost-comparator:v1`). Copy-report emits a paste-ready markdown handoff. **Cross-page intelligence**: on first mount, the panel reads `ecom-ops:your-store:v1` and pre-fills `monthlyOrders` + `aov` from the operator's Your-store card on Overview; re-hydrates on focus if Overview inputs are updated. Sidebar nav entry was already present at `/inventory`.
- **Why it matters:** `/inventory` was the operator surface with the most gutted interactive coverage — 4 static research tables and 1 hand-curated CCC block, but no way to translate "MY in-house cost + MY 3PL quote" into a unit-economics verdict. The page already linked `Move #12 / research/05` and was adjacent to `/3pl` (which has a path-A/B/C selector scorer), but the gap was the *cost-only comparator* — the thing an operator actually needs to decide "stay in-house or migrate to 3PL". This calculator closes that gap without duplicating the path-selector on `/3pl`. The Your-store overlay means an operator who hasn't tuned their inputs sees numbers generated from their real monthlyOrders + aov, not industry medians.
- **Files added:** `dashboard/src/lib/inventory-cost-comparator.ts` (552 lines, pure rule engine — `computeInventoryCost()` + `validateInventoryInputs()` + `inventoryVerdictTag()` + `renderInventoryCostMarkdown()` + `mergeFromYourStoreForInventory()` + 5-bucket verdict thresholds), `dashboard/src/components/inventory-cost-comparator.tsx` (685 lines, client component with 10 in-house + 4 3PL input fields + side-by-side cost-stack output + 4-metric delta bar + verdict tag + copy report), `dashboard/src/lib/__tests__/inventory-cost-comparator.test.ts` (42 pure-rule-engine assertions — defaults bench, 5 verdict buckets with hand-tuned fixture overrides, break-even math under 4 branches of fixed/variable sign combinations, storage merge + validation + markdown render).
- **Files modified:** `dashboard/app/inventory/page.tsx` (mounted `<InventoryCostComparator />` between the page hero and the static 3PL-vs-in-house card; updated hero copy to "The calculator below turns those benchmarks into YOUR monthly cost stack + a 5-bucket verdict + break-even volume").

## 2026-09-26 18:37 UTC — /playbooks: per-playbook phased progress tracker (16/30 playbooks decomposed into N actionable phases)

- **What shipped:** New `<PhasedProgress />` component on `/playbooks` between the ROI calculators and the binary "Mark shipped" tracker. Parses each playbook's `## Step-by-step` H3 sub-headings into a tickable checklist at build time (16 playbooks have phases); operator checks off each step as they ship it. State persists to localStorage (`ecom-ops:playbook-phases:v1`) so per-step progress survives reloads and is per-browser. Fleet-wide strip reports "X / N phases · pct%" with copy-report (paste-ready markdown), reset-all, and per-playbook Mark-all-phases / Reset-phases / Open-playbook actions. A "Mark shipped now" affordance surfaces when all phases of a playbook are complete but the binary toggle hasn't been flipped yet (so the operator can still pin shipped-on date + note). Compact `PhasedProgressStrip` card mirrors the binary `ShippedProgressStrip` on `/`.
- **Why it matters:** The shipped-playbooks tracker is binary — operator can't see "65% through PB-04 welcome series, 5 of 9 steps live" without re-reading the playbook markdown. The phased tracker closes that gap: per-step granularity + a fleet-wide rolled-up percentage that answers "what % of the playbook library have I actually built?" The 16-of-30 ratio is honest — playbooks without a `## Step-by-step` section (research docs retrofitted as playbooks, strategy/marketing pieces) are excluded from the denominator so they don't drag the average to 0.

## 2026-09-27 18:10 UTC — /inventory Stockout-risk calculator (interactive-tool + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence)

- **What shipped:** New interactive calculator mounted on `/inventory` between the 3PL-vs-In-house Cost Comparator and the reference tables. The /inventory page historically surfaced only static research tables (3PL vs in-house cost stack + Major 3PLs pricing + forecasting basics + CCC); the calculator turns it into the operator's actual weekly-stockout dashboard. 8 inputs: monthlyOrders + AOV + gross margin (auto-filled from `ecom-ops:your-store:v1` on Overview — cross-page intelligence) + onHandUnits + weeklySellThroughPct + supplierLeadTimeDays + safetyStockWeeks + reorderCadenceDays + wholesaleCostPctOfAov. Outputs: weeks-of-stock + expected-stockout-in-days + reorder-arrival-window + days-of-cover-gap (positive = stockout risk) + lost-orders-if-stockout + lost-revenue-if-stockout + lost-margin-if-stockout + recommended PO size + wholesale PO cost + annual-carry-cost estimate + a 5-band verdict (STOCKOUT IMMINENT / TIGHT — REORDER THIS WEEK / WATCH / HEALTHY / OVERSTOCKED — CAPITAL DRAG). Reorder-now flag fires when reorder arrival window > expected stockout date. Copy-audit-report button emits a paste-ready markdown report (standup / Notion / Slack). Persistence: `ecom-ops:stockout-risk:v1` (full inputs map); "Save as my numbers" button opts into persistence (defaults don't auto-save so the operator who just landed from the nav doesn't get their visitor-state committed before they intend).
- **Why it matters:** Closes the second of two gaps on `/inventory` (3PL cost comparator already shipped; stockout math wasn't). The canonical DTC inventory rule — "if reorder arrival > cover, you're losing orders" — is currently buried in a research table with no operator-facing calculator. This calculator turns the rule into a per-operator verdict: at the canonical $1M-GMV apparel defaults (1,000 orders/mo, $75 AOV, 2,000 on-hand, 25% sell-through/wk, 21d lead, 14d cadence, 2wk buffer) the math fires "STOCKOUT IMMINENT" (4-week cover ≤ 28d arrival window). Cross-tab + same-tab sync means updating Your-store on Overview while viewing /inventory triggers a re-hydration without a remount.
- **Where to see it:** https://ecommerce-ops-iota.vercel.app/inventory — the stockout-risk card sits right below the 3PL cost comparator; AOV/orders/margin fields auto-fill from Your-store on first mount. Or click "Save as my numbers" to persist a specific scenario (e.g. entering your real lead time + sell-through for SKB-12 hoodie).
- **Feature class:** interactive-tool + state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence + one-click-action (copy audit)

## 2026-09-28 20:00 UTC — /loyalty-launch-plan: 30-day always-on Loyalty Program launch plan generator (Move #8)

- **What shipped:** New route at `/loyalty-launch-plan` with a one-click "Generate 30-day launch plan" button. Opens a modal with a 30-day day-by-day checklist (Days 1–30 across W1–W4) generated from the operator's saved Loyalty ROI calculator inputs (`ecom-ops:playbooks:loyalty-roi:v1`) overlaid with their Your-store AOV/orders/margin (`ecom-ops:your-store:v1`). Snapshot block (verdict + net revenue / month + net per $1 program + payback months) computed by `forecastLoyalty()` — same math as `playbooks/07-loyalty-program-smile.md`. Result is paste-ready markdown: copy-to-clipboard OR download `.md` (named `loyalty-launch-plan-YYYY-MM-DD.md`). 30 days, 4 weeks, 30 checkbox-able actions covering: app install + points/tiers/referral config + Klaviyo webhook wiring + Triple Whale cohort overlay (W1); 6-touch launch sequence build (3 emails + 3 SMS) + on-site widget + post-purchase + account-page embed + win-back flow for non-enrolled (W2); soft-launch to 10% then ramp to 50% / 100% + D-7 / D-14 / D-21 enrollment-rate readouts + support-team briefing (W3); 90-day repeat-rate proxy + payback-month readout + iteration backlog + Q2 priorities + 30-day program readout deck (W4). CTA button also surfaced on the Loyalty ROI calculator on `/playbooks/07-loyalty-program-smile` (next to "Reset defaults" and "Copy report") for at-handbook discovery. Sidebar nav entry added (icon ▦).

- **Why it matters:** Companion to the 3 existing launch-plan generators (PDP A/B, Welcome Series, Abandoned-Cart) — closes the same gap for the second-largest retention-lever program. Operators typically have the 3-tier VIP + 6-touch launch sequence template ready in Smile.io / Yotpo / LoyaltyLion but no calendar-paced checklist to drive the launch. The plan reads the operator's REAL existing-customer base / AOV / margin / enrollment-rate / expected-lift so a $500k DTC operator who hasn't tweaked the calc gets the plan generated from their real numbers, not the 5,000-customer / $75-AOV / 25%-baseline / +7-pts / 60%-enrollment / $249/mo Smile.io Growth / $60/mo overhead defaults. Cross-page intelligence: reads from both `loyalty-roi:v1` and `your-store:v1` so the snapshot is consistent across Overview, Playbooks, and the launch-plan route. The 90-day repeat-rate lift (+5 to +9 pts over baseline) is only achievable if the operator wires the Klaviyo + Postscript + Triple Whale + Smile stack in the right order; the plan enforces that ordering so the +5 pts lift isn't accidentally misattributed to the welcome series.

- **What shipped:** New route at `/checkout-audit-launch-plan` with a one-click "Generate 30-day launch plan" button. Opens a modal with a 30-day day-by-day checklist (Days 1–30 across W1–W4) generated from the operator's saved Baymard audit inputs (`ecom-ops:cro:checkout-audit:v1`). Snapshot block (current 0–100 Baymard score + health band + cumulative CVR-lift band, capped at +80%) computed by `scoreAudit()` — same math as `scripts/checkout_audit_score.py` + `dashboard/src/lib/checkout-audit.ts`. Result is paste-ready markdown: copy-to-clipboard OR download `.md` (named `checkout-audit-launch-plan-YYYY-MM-DD.md`). 30 days, 4 weeks, 30 checkbox-able actions covering: Severity L baseline + 5 highest-lift fixes (guest checkout, Shop Pay + Apple Pay + Google Pay, address autocomplete, single-page checkout, sticky place-order, real shipping cost upfront); Severity M fixes (minimum fields, inline validation, BNPL for AOV > $150, payment icons, trust badges, no guest redirect, touch-targets ≥44×44, 16px input fonts); Severity S polish (no password meter, visible field labels, inline errors, secure-checkout lock, returns-policy link, cross-browser audit); E5 real-device test + score-after-W3 + +CVR-lift proxy computation + Move #4 (mobile-PDP) cross-link + 30-day readout deck. CTA button also surfaced on `/cro` next to the Baymard audit card for at-handbook discovery. Sidebar nav entry added (icon ▦). The plan enforces W1 = Severity L only, so shipping the W1 plan alone moves the audit from weak/fair to good / great.

- **Why it matters:** Companion to the 9 existing launch-plan generators (PDP A/B #9.5, Welcome Series #3.4, Abandoned Cart #1, Loyalty #8, Post-Purchase Upsell #9.6, SMS-WC #6, Attribution-Alert #6.10, Subscription #11, 3PL #52) — closes the same gap for Move #3, the highest-CVR-leverage lever. The plan reads the operator's REAL audit state (current pass / partial / fail / skip / missing per guideline) so a $3M DTC operator who hasn't run the audit gets the plan generated from the missing-audit baseline (0/100 score, +80% CVR-lift ceiling), not industry placeholders. ## 2026-09-30 21:55 UTC — /master-rollout-calendar: 90-day multi-move Master Rollout Calendar generator + collision detection + .ics export (Move #N)

- **What shipped:** New route at `/master-rollout-calendar` with a one-click "Generate 90-day Master Rollout Calendar" button. Opens a modal that reads ALL 9 per-move calculator localStorage keys (`ecom-ops:playbooks:ac-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:ws-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:loyalty-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:ppu-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:sms-wc-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:pdp-ab:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:attribution-alert:v1` + `ecom-ops:subscription-path:v1` + `ecom-ops:playbooks:threepl:v1` + `ecom-ops:cro:checkout-audit:v1`) plus `ecom-ops:your-store:v1`, sequences all 10 launches in canonical foundation → revenue → CRO → retention build order (Phase 1: SMS-WC + Welcome Series; Phase 2: Abandoned Cart + Post-Purchase Upsell; Phase 3: PDP A/B + Checkout Audit; Phase 4: Loyalty + Subscription + Attribution-Alert + 3PL), detects 3 kinds of collisions (klaviyo-sms-collision, klaviyo-email-collision, staff-constraint-collision), sums combined Year-1 net margin + cost across all 10 moves, computes combined ROI + health band. Result is a gantt-style 90-day markdown checklist + RFC 5545 .ics (one all-day event per move). Copy-to-clipboard + download `.md` + download `.ics`. Day-1 start date is operator-pickable (defaults to today); cross-tab sync via `storage` event so editing a calculator in another tab re-hydrates this calendar.

- **Why it matters:** Companion to the 9 existing launch-plan generators — closes the cross-move operational sequencing gap. The 9 per-move launch-plan generators each take the operator's per-move inputs and emit a 30-day markdown checklist. That works per-move, but the operator who has run 3-4 generators now has 60-120 days of un-sequenced work: what do they ship first? Which moves collide on Klaviyo / Postscript / SMS / ops in the same week? What's the combined Year-1 ROI? This page is the cross-move view: it walks the catalog in canonical build order (foundation first, retention last), detects same-week build collisions on Klaviyo / Klaviyo-SMS / staff-constraint with severity levels (info / warn / block), sums the per-move Year-1 net margin + cost into a combined ROI rollup (default Year-1 industry combined ROI ≈ 20:1 across the 10 moves, $895k net margin, $63k cost), and emits a single calendar-ready file the operator imports into Google Calendar / Apple Calendar / Outlook as colored all-day bands. Companion to `/30-day-plan` (single-move synthesis doc).

## 2026-10-01 05:30 UTC — /launch-plan-progress: cross-page-intelligence progress tracker for all 10 launch-plan generators (Move #N.2)

- **What shipped:** New route at `/launch-plan-progress` with an interactive 30-day × 10-plan grid tracker. Each of the 10 launch-plan pages (`/pdp-ab-launch-plan`, `/welcome-series-launch-plan`, `/abandoned-cart-launch-plan`, `/loyalty-launch-plan`, `/post-purchase-upsell-launch-plan`, `/sms-welcome-cart-launch-plan`, `/attribution-health-alert-launch-plan`, `/subscription-launch-plan`, `/3pl-launch-plan`, `/checkout-audit-launch-plan`) gets a per-plan card with: (a) clickable day cells (30 days per plan, click to mark shipped / un-shipped), (b) per-plan progress bar with W1/W2/W3/W4 completion counts, (c) health band ("complete" / "on-track" ≥60% / "started" 1–59% / "untouched" 0%), (d) first/last shipped date, (e) realised Year-1 net margin against the per-move default benchmark, (f) Reset button per plan. Top of page: aggregate rollup card (total days shipped, % completion, total realised Y1 margin, health band counts) + Copy/Download markdown buttons for the standup-ready rollup block. State persisted per-browser to `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:v1` (cross-tab sync via `storage` event; cross-component notify via custom `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:update` event).

- **Why it matters:** Closes the post-generation visibility gap for the 9 existing launch-plan generators. Operators today click "Generate" → get a markdown → paste into Linear / Notion / Slack → lose visibility into how many days they've actually shipped. This page is the operator-facing rollup: one tick box per action, one progress bar per plan, one aggregate card at the top. The realised-vs-default margin display makes the standup summary immediately CFO-readable (e.g. "$147,000 of $1,278,000 realised Y1 margin across the 10 plans = 11.5% shipped"). ## 2026-10-02 02:30 UTC — /launch-plan-progress: per-day ship notes full-text search (Move #N.4)

- **What shipped:** New full-text search panel on `/launch-plan-progress`. Operators type a query (single term, multi-term AND-joined, or quoted phrase) and get ranked, highlighted results across every note attached to a ticked day on all 10 launch-plan pages. Each hit shows: plan title pill (links to the per-plan tracker), day number, shipped-date, match-count, and a context snippet with the matched substring wrapped in a `<mark>` highlight. Suggested-query chips (`blocked`, `Klaviyo`, `Shop Pay`, `"legal review"`, `pending`, `"brand team"`) populate the input for one-click common workflows. Copy/Download buttons emit a paste-ready markdown block (per-plan, per-day: `- **<title>** — Day N (YYYY-MM-DD): <note>`) for the matched subset.

- **Why it matters:** Closes the post-generation WHERE/WHO/WHAT gap for the 10 launch-plan generators. Operators ship days → attach notes ("Day 5 blocked: Klaviyo template QA held by brand team"). Within a few weeks the 280-char notes become a real corpus — and a standup reader or an incident responder needs to ask "find every 'blocked' mention", "find every note mentioning the brand lead", "every reference to Klaviyo across all 10 plans" in a single search. Move #N.4 wires a full-text search layer over the same localStorage map the notes overlay writes (`ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress-notes:v1` + cross-references `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:v1` to scope the index to actually-ticked days).

## 2026-10-03 10:00 UTC — Move #N.7 per-playbook realized-ROI ledger

- **What shipped:** New per-playbook actual-revenue tracker. Operator opens any shipped playbook on `/playbooks/[slug]` and clicks **Log actual revenue** → types in $/month revenue lift, $/month cost, orders recovered, measurement window, confidence (low/medium/high), and a 500-char note → saves to `ecom-ops:realized-roi:v1`. Summary tile renders net monthly lift, annualized, ROI multiple (handles `∞×` when cost=0), orders recovered, plus a **gap-vs-projected** badge (UNDERWIDE / UNDER / ON-TARGET / OVER / UNMEASURED) once a projection band is supplied. The Overview at `/` shows a compact rollup: total entries logged, net monthly / annualized, average ROI multiple, total orders recovered, plus a 3-tile breakdown of underperforming / on-target / outperforming.

- **Why it matters:** Closes the canonical "projected-vs-actual gap" problem. The existing `RealizedRoiPanel` shows PROJECTED annual lift (the canonical per-move monthly-lift-band table × shipped map). Most operators never write down what they ACTUALLY captured, so the dashboard is honest about projections but blind to results. Move #N.7 lets the operator close the loop: ship → measure → log → see the gap. The UNDERWIDE badge is the load-bearing signal — a playbook that's <25% of projected means the playbook either isn't working OR the projection was wrong; either way the operator needs to know now, not in the next quarterly review.

- **Feature class:** state-persistence + cross-page-intelligence + one-click-action (per-playbook form → localStorage → cross-tab `storage` event → same-tab `ecom-ops:realized-roi:update` CustomEvent → rollup on `/`)

- **What shipped:** Cross-page-intelligence Lifecycle Fleet Health card on `/` Overview. ## 2026-10-04 00:33 UTC — Move #N.9 Operator action digest on /today

- **What shipped:** Cross-page-intelligence card on `/today` synthesizing state from 4 storage keys (`ecom-ops:shipped-playbooks:v1` + `ecom-ops:realized-roi:v1` + `ecom-ops:lifecycle-flow-health:v1` + `ecom-ops:your-store:v1`) + the build-time Top-10 + playbook catalog into a single prioritized ordered checklist with deep-anchor links. The card sits between `CronHealthCard` (system status) and `NextMoveCard` (cron's pick) so the operator sees their personal queue right after the daily cockpit header — before scrolling past the ROI calculators below. Five priority classes — `BLOCK` (P0, red) / `ACT` (P1, amber) / `LOG` (P2, sky) / `EDIT` (P3, violet) — with a kind-tinted chip per action + per-action reason text + metric chip showing the canonical number that fired the rule (e.g. "Score: 32/100", "Confidence: low", "Move: pending"). The card renders a 4-tile priority-counts strip ("X BLOCK · Y ACT · Z LOG · W EDIT") showing the **uncapped** count even when the action list itself caps at 8 rows.

- **Why it matters:** Closes the canonical "I have 6 tabs open and don't know what to work on" gap. The Today page has had KPIs + Your-store + IkasLiveCard + CronHealthCard + 3 ROI calculators + Trajectory panels + a "Today's focus" quote from the cron-picked next move + a "what shipped" 3-tick recap, but never answered "given YOUR specific state across 4 storage keys, what's your highest-urgency next action?" The digest reads them all and produces the prioritized queue. P0 BLOCK rules surface the bleeding-revenue issues (a Lifecycle FAIL flow, a low-confidence realized-ROI entry) — the operator can't see those anywhere else without manually opening `/lifecycle` + `/playbooks/<id>`. P1 ACT rules surface the highest-leverage next moves (Top-10 pending queue, Lifecycle NEEDS_WORK). P2 LOG rules surface the projection-vs-actual gap (shipped playbooks with no logged actuals, or low-confidence entries that need re-logging). P3 EDIT rules surface the "your-store is on defaults, your numbers aren't projecting" anti-pattern. Empty-state CTA: "You're on track" with "Open Next Move →" link when every axis is engaged AND zero actions remain (the canonical "don't render an empty 0-todo widget" anti-pattern).

- **Feature class:** cross-page-intelligence + state-persistence (reads 4 storage keys; no separate storage key for the digest itself) + interactive-tool (kind-tinted chips + copy-as-Slack Markdown button + priority-counts strip drive visual triage). One-click-action via the per-row → deep anchor (each action is a real link to the operator's next click).

## 2026-10-04 12:48 UTC — Move #N.10 Next-move SROI ($/day) ranking + sort toggle

- **What shipped:** Per-move **SROI (Speed-of-Return-On-Investment)** scoring on the next-move card. SROI = projected monthly lift midpoint ÷ days-to-ship, computed live against Your-store's monthly revenue. Every Top-10 move gets a SROI ($/day) badge + a SROI rank (1 = highest $/day). The compare-table gains a new **sort toggle** ("Priority" / "$/day (SROI)") — when the operator picks SROI mode, the table re-sorts by $/day desc (priorityRank is the stable tie-break), shows a per-row "SROI rank" pill (#N/10), and a header pill "Best $/day: Move #X — $Y/d". A new **SROI pill** in the card header (next to the Move #X pill) surfaces the recommended move's $/day + rank on first load. The sort preference persists in `ecom-ops:next-move-sort:v1` and survives reloads + cross-tab sync (storage event + same-tab `ecom-ops:next-move-sort:update` CustomEvent).

- **Why it matters:** Closes the canonical "algorithmic #1 isn't always the right #1" gap. The existing priorityRank recommender is right that Move #1 (abandoned cart) has the highest lift band — but Move #1 ships in 3 days at $0-60/mo cost, so the SROI is ~$2.5k/d at $75k/mo baseline; Move #3 (checkout audit) ships in 5 days with 20-35% lift and **$0 cost**, so the SROI is ~$3.75k/d at $75k/mo baseline — 50% higher $/day. For a $1M GMV operator, both produce huge lift, but the operator's first question after "what should I ship?" is "what pays back fastest?" — SROI answers it. The new toggle preserves the algorithmic #1 (the priority pill + SROI pill both still surface the recommended move) but lets the operator re-compare on a different axis. The **breakeven column** (days for projected lift to cover monthly cost) is the second axis — a move with high SROI but high cost (Move #9 mobile PDP redesign: $1-3k/mo tooling × 14d shipping) has a much longer breakeven than a zero-cost move with lower SROI.

- **Feature class:** cross-page-intelligence (reads Your-store + shipped-playbooks + override + sort-pref; writes sort-pref) + state-persistence (`ecom-ops:next-move-sort:v1` survives reloads + cross-tab) + interactive-tool (sort toggle re-sorts table + recomputes per-row badges live).

- **Files added:** `dashboard/src/lib/next-move-sroi.ts` (~270 lines: pure-logic `computeNextMoveSroi(move, monthlyRev)` returning `{liftLowUsd, liftHighUsd, liftMidUsd, costMidUsd, daysToShip, sroiUsdPerDay, netSroiUsdPerDay, breakevenDays, sroiRank}`; ## 2026-10-04 19:08 UTC — Move #N.11 Shipping activity heatmap on /launch-plan-progress

- **What shipped:** Cross-page-intelligence temporal view of launch-plan shipping on `/launch-plan-progress`. The tracker records WHICH (plan, day) pair shipped; this widget turns the same `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:v1` localStorage key into a GitHub-style 13-week activity heatmap plus the 4 momentum metrics operators actually need to know. Five panels: (1) **Momentum strip** with 4 tiles — current streak, longest streak, last ship ("today" / "yesterday" / "5 days ago" / "—"), velocity (7d vs 30d) as "accelerating" / "steady" / "slowing" / "stalled" / "idle" / "new"; (2) **30/60/90-day windows** with progress bars + counts; (3) **13×7 heatmap grid** (91 days ending today, 5-level intensity bucket 0 ships→muted / 1→faint / 2→light / 3-4→medium / 5+→deep emerald, future cells dimmed 30%, per-cell tooltip with date + ship count + plan count, month labels in the column header); (4) **Weekday breakdown** — Mon..Sun totals + per-weekday active-days + shipping rate; (5) **Recent ship days list** — newest-first up to 14 cells with ship count + which plans shipped (PDP A/B / Welcome / etc.). Plus a 5-cell legend (Less → More), a "Less intensity 0/1/2/3/4 → More" with colour squares, and a storage-key footer reading `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:v1`.

- **Why it matters:** Closes the canonical "I shipped 6 things but I don't know if I'm on a streak" gap. The launch-plan tracker has 10 plans × 30 days = 300 day cells, but the per-plan progress bar only answers "what % of plan X am I at" — it can't answer "did I ship anything this week?" The new heatmap answers the temporal questions every operator asks their dashboard: "am I on a streak?", "when did I last ship?", "am I accelerating or slowing?", "what days of the week do I actually ship?". The velocity tile (7d vs 30d) is the load-bearing metric — a single number that tells you whether the launch is gaining or losing steam without scrolling through 300 cells.

- **Feature class:** cross-page-intelligence (reads `/launch-plan-progress`'s tracker localStorage; no separate storage key — pure consumer of the existing one) + state-persistence (cross-tab `storage` event + same-tab `ecom-ops:launch-plan-progress:update` custom event) + interactive-tool (5-level heatmap intensity + per-cell tooltip + per-weekday rate bars + copy/download markdown export). Pure-logic helpers are testable in isolation; component is hydration-safe (SSR renders the empty-state stub, client hydrates from localStorage on mount).

## 2026-10-05 01:20 UTC — Move #N.12 Per-flow fix recipe drilldown on /lifecycle

- **What shipped:** New `<FlowFixRecipeCard />` on `/lifecycle` (mounted below the audit panel) that turns every failed lifecycle flow into a **prioritized fix recipe**. Two views: (1) **All-flows table** — verdict badge · score · failed-gate count · top-fix gate · top-fix SROI · $ at risk /mo · click-to-drill, sorted FAIL → NEEDS_WORK → WARN → PASS; (2) **Per-flow drilldown** (auto-shown when the URL has `/lifecycle#<flow-id>`, e.g. from Move #N.9's P0 BLOCK deep-link) — 3-tile summary (top-fix $/1k sent + SROI + total $ at risk) + "Read first" playbook card + prioritized gate-fix list (ranked by expected lift $/1k sent desc, SROI tie-break) with measured message + diagnostic Klaviyo/Postscript tab + 1-3 concrete changes per gate + "Copy recipe" markdown export.

- **Why it matters:** Closes the canonical "I clicked the /lifecycle#1.1_browse_abandon deep-link from /today but the page just showed me a score and 6 error messages — which gate do I fix first, what does the fix look like, and how much is it worth?" gap. Move #N.9's P0 BLOCK actions list FAIL flows; Move #N.12 lands the operator on a concrete, prioritized recipe. **The sort is the load-bearing decision**: not all failed gates are equal. A FAIL on Gate E (revenue) recovers 300-2500 $/1k sent but takes 2 days; a FAIL on Gate A (subject/send-time) recovers 50-200 $/1k sent but takes 0.25d — the SROI math ($/day) tells the operator which to ship FIRST. Per-gate effort is pinned (0.25/0.5/1/2d) so the prioritization is reproducible, not vibes.

- **Feature class:** interactive-tool (sortable table + click-to-drill + copy-recipe markdown) + cross-page-intelligence (reads `/lifecycle` audit's localStorage + same flow_id hash as Move #N.9 emits; writes nothing — pure consumer) + state-persistence (cross-tab `storage` + same-tab `ecom-ops:lifecycle-flow-health:update` CustomEvent sync).
